:::{#thm-surprisal-chain-rule}
#### Chain rule for surprisal

For discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$
and outcomes $x$ and $y$ with $\P(X=x, Y=y) > 0$,

$$s(x, y) = s(x) + s(y \mid x).$$

:::

::: {.proof}

Since $\P(X=x, Y=y) = \P(X=x) \, \P(Y=y \mid X=x)$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
s(x, y)
&= -\log \P(X=x, Y=y) \\
&= -\log \sb{\P(X=x) \, \P(Y=y \mid X=x)} \\
&= -\log \P(X=x) - \log \P(Y=y \mid X=x) \\
&= s(x) + s(y \mid x).
\end{aligned}
$$

:::
